Score a throw of five dice in one of the twelve categories of the dice game Yacht.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/yacht) (MIT). Listed under [Games & Simulation](/examples/?subject=games-and-simulation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: yacht.nomi
//# Scores a throw of five dice in the dice game Yacht.

/// The twelve ways to score a throw of five dice.
pub enum Category {
    Ones
    Twos
    Threes
    Fours
    Fives
    Sixes
    FullHouse
    FourOfAKind
    LittleStraight
    BigStraight
    Choice
    Yacht
}

/// The score of five `dice` in `category`: 0 when they do not make it.
pub fn score(dice: List<Int>, category: Category) -> Int {
    case category {
        .Ones -> face_total(dice, 1)
        .Twos -> face_total(dice, 2)
        .Threes -> face_total(dice, 3)
        .Fours -> face_total(dice, 4)
        .Fives -> face_total(dice, 5)
        .Sixes -> face_total(dice, 6)
        .FullHouse -> full_house(dice)
        .FourOfAKind -> four_of_a_kind(dice)
        .LittleStraight -> straight(dice, from: 1)
        .BigStraight -> straight(dice, from: 2)
        .Choice -> Iter.sum(dice)
        .Yacht -> yacht(dice)
    }
}

/// The total of the dice showing `face`.
fn face_total(dice: List<Int>, face: Int) -> Int {
    count = dice |> Iter.filter(&(&1 == face)) |> Iter.count()
    face * count
}

/// All the dice when three show one face and two another, or 0.
fn full_house(dice: List<Int>) -> Int {
    if group_sizes(dice) == [2, 3] {
        Iter.sum(dice)
    } else {
        0
    }
}

/// Four times the face that at least four dice show, or 0.
fn four_of_a_kind(dice: List<Int>) -> Int {
    dice
    |> Iter.frequencies()
    |> Iter.find(fn #(_face, count) -> count >= 4)
    |> Maybe.map(fn #(face, _count) -> 4 * face)
    |> Maybe.with_default(0)
}

/// 30 when the dice are the five faces counting up `from`, or 0.
fn straight(dice: List<Int>, from: Int) -> Int {
    if Iter.sort(dice) == Iter.to_list(from..from + 5) {
        30
    } else {
        0
    }
}

/// 50 when all five dice show one face, or 0.
fn yacht(dice: List<Int>) -> Int {
    if group_sizes(dice) == [5] { 50 } else { 0 }
}

/// How many dice show each face that comes up, smallest group first: a full
/// house is `[2, 3]`, a yacht `[5]`.
fn group_sizes(dice: List<Int>) -> List<Int> {
    dice
    |> Iter.frequencies()
    |> Map.values()
    |> Iter.sort()
}

// FILE: yacht_test.nomi
import yacht.{self, Category}

test "yacht" {
    cases = [
        #("Yacht", [5, 5, 5, 5, 5], Category.Yacht, 50),
        #("Not Yacht", [1, 3, 3, 2, 5], .Yacht, 0),
        #("Ones", [1, 1, 1, 3, 5], .Ones, 3),
        #("Ones, out of order", [3, 1, 1, 5, 1], .Ones, 3),
        #("No ones", [4, 3, 6, 5, 5], .Ones, 0),
        #("Twos", [2, 3, 4, 5, 6], .Twos, 2),
        #("Fours", [1, 4, 1, 4, 1], .Fours, 8),
        #("Yacht counted as threes", [3, 3, 3, 3, 3], .Threes, 15),
        #("Yacht of 3s counted as fives", [3, 3, 3, 3, 3], .Fives, 0),
        #("Fives", [1, 5, 3, 5, 3], .Fives, 10),
        #("Sixes", [2, 3, 4, 5, 6], .Sixes, 6),
        #("Full house two small, three big", [2, 2, 4, 4, 4], .FullHouse, 16),
        #("Full house three small, two big", [5, 3, 3, 5, 3], .FullHouse, 19),
        #("Two pair is not a full house", [2, 2, 4, 4, 5], .FullHouse, 0),
        #("Four of a kind is not a full house", [1, 4, 4, 4, 4], .FullHouse, 0),
        #("Yacht is not a full house", [2, 2, 2, 2, 2], .FullHouse, 0),
        #("Four of a Kind", [6, 6, 4, 6, 6], .FourOfAKind, 24),
        #("Yacht can be scored as Four of a Kind", [3, 3, 3, 3, 3], .FourOfAKind, 12),
        #("Full house is not Four of a Kind", [3, 3, 3, 5, 5], .FourOfAKind, 0),
        #("Little Straight", [3, 5, 4, 1, 2], .LittleStraight, 30),
        #("Little Straight as Big Straight", [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], .BigStraight, 0),
        #("Four in order but not a little straight", [1, 1, 2, 3, 4], .LittleStraight, 0),
        #("No pairs but not a little straight", [1, 2, 3, 4, 6], .LittleStraight, 0),
        #(
            "Minimum is 1, maximum is 5, but not a little straight",
            [1, 1, 3, 4, 5],
            .LittleStraight,
            0,
        ),
        #("Big Straight", [4, 6, 2, 5, 3], .BigStraight, 30),
        #("Big Straight as little straight", [6, 5, 4, 3, 2], .LittleStraight, 0),
        #("No pairs but not a big straight", [6, 5, 4, 3, 1], .BigStraight, 0),
        #("Choice", [3, 3, 5, 6, 6], .Choice, 23),
        #("Yacht as choice", [2, 2, 2, 2, 2], .Choice, 10),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, dice, category, expected), description {
        assert yacht.score(dice, category) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The categories are an enum, `Category`, and `score` is one `case` over it, so a category without a score is a missing arm. The canonical strings (`"full house"`) are the test table's data, written as variants: the first row qualifies `Category.Yacht` and the rows after it are bare.
- The dice are a `List<Int>`, as the canonical data gives them.
- Several categories ask for a shape, not particular faces. `group_sizes` answers how many dice show each face that comes up, sorted: `Iter.frequencies`, then the map's values, then `Iter.sort`. A full house is `[2, 3]` and a yacht `[5]`, whatever the faces are.
- The straights compare the sorted dice with the five faces counting up from 1 or from 2, built as a range, `Iter.to_list(from..from + 5)`; `from` is a named argument at the call, `straight(dice, from: 1)`.
- Four of a kind finds the face that four or more dice show with `Iter.find` over the frequencies, so a yacht scores as four of a kind too. No such face is a real answer, scored 0, so `Maybe.with_default(0)` is the rule, not a guess.
- Each category that is made or not is its own function, so every arm of `score` is one call and stays on one line; an `if` in an arm breaks past the formatter's one-line width and takes every arm with it.
- The 29 canonical cases are one `subtests` table named by the description column.
